Subject: RE: Production — sustained 5xx/throughput degradation during ramp

Naomi / Redwood team,

We're seeing recurring request rejections and latency spikes starting ~08:45 PDT this morning as we ramp up pre-Black Friday test traffic. Key observations: 503 and 429 responses across multiple endpoints, tail latency jumping to 1.1s -> 2.3s, and effective throughput dropped ~40% for our realtime inference route. Attached is a short snapshot of request traces and a token-level histogram (traffic_snapshot-20290510.json).

This is blocking our smoke tests for the BFCM promo. Can you confirm whether this is an application-level regression or a platform-side throttle (rate limiting / quota / burst behavior)? We need urgency here — please advise on mitigation steps and whether you can temporarily relax limits for our account while we test.

We're standing up our on-call and can jump into a war room.

Thanks,
Evan Roberts
Head of Platform Operations
Greenline Retail

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evan Roberts <evan.roberts@greenline-retail.com>
Date: Fri, 10 May 2029 10:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production — sustained 5xx/throughput degradation during ramp

Investigating — quick findings below. Reproduced with internal load generator against GL tenant.

Root cause (prelim): per-tenant burst token bucket misconfiguration. The policy for this tier is supposed to allow a 60s smoothing window with a modest additional burst credit; however, a regression in our policy materialization pipeline set the burst window to 1s and the refill rate to the per-second baseline. Net effect: legitimate short-duration QPS spikes exhausted tokens immediately, triggering our suppression logic and rapid fallback that surfaces to the customer as 429s and, in some proxy paths, 503s.

Immediate mitigation applied at 10:02 PDT: temporarily increased the burst window to 60s and bumped burst tokens x4 for tenant GL-67890. Early signs: enforcement events dropped ~85% in the next 5 minutes and throughput recovered to ~95% of baseline. Rolling a config hotfix now to ensure the policy materializes correctly across regions.

Follow-ups:
- I'll open an INF ticket to patch the materializer and add an automated test to assert window length parity.
- We should coordinate a customer-facing timeline and an offer for remediation credits (Marissa/Laura).
- Postmortem with timeline, RCA, and preventive actions.

I'll update when the hotfix is live globally.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Sr. SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Greenline — summary, mitigation, and next steps (action required)

Evan — apologies again for the disruption during your traffic ramp. Below is a concise summary and the actions we've taken plus next steps.

Summary:
- Incident window: 2029-05-10 08:44 — 09:10 PDT (initial enforcement spike).
- Impact: elevated 429/503 responses on realtime endpoints; peak tail latency ~2.3s; throughput down ~40% for ~20m.
- Root cause (prelim): a policy materialization regression set per-tenant burst window to 1s instead of 60s, causing legitimate QPS bursts to exhaust tokens and trigger suppression.

Actions taken:
1) Immediate mitigation (2029-05-10 10:02 PDT): temporarily increased burst window to 60s and bumped burst tokens x4 for GL-67890 — observed enforcement event reduction ~85% and throughput recovery to ~95%.
2) Hotfix deployed (2029-05-10 11:00 PDT): patch to materializer to prevent incorrect window lengths from being pushed. Global rollout completed 2029-05-10 11:48 PDT.
3) Remediation plan: INF-2458 created to add unit/integration tests for materializer, and an alert that surfaces sudden divergence between configured policy and materialized policy per tenant.

Customer-facing commitments:
- We will host a dedicated SRE war room for your next ramp window and provide a postmortem within 72 hours (expected 2029-05-13 EOD PST).
- As a goodwill gesture we propose a 2-month credit (see attached proposal). Please confirm accept/decline and any preferred logistics for the war room.

Next steps for Redwood (owner):
- Marcus: confirm INF ticket and ETA for automated tests.
- Marissa/Laura: confirm commercial concession and customer communication draft.
- Naomi: deliver postmortem and exec brief to both customer and our leadership.

Attached: traffic_snapshot-20290510.json, burst_policy_v1.pdf, Greenline_MVP_MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN.xlsx

Evan — I'll set up a short call if you'd like to walk through the technical details; otherwise we'll send the 72-hour postmortem as promised.

— Naomi Feldman

Redwood Inference
